name: Steak tartare with potato chips & gem lettuce

source.author: Instagram (English, pasted text) — 'The Tartare Series' ep. 1
source.notes: Classic steak tartare: hand-diced semi-frozen beef dressed with an emulsified Dijon-lemon-olive-oil dressing, shallot, gherkins, capers, parsley, Tabasco and Worcestershire, topped with a RAW egg yolk and chives; served with deep-fried homemade potato chips and gem lettuce cups. Analyzed as 2 servings with a lean tartare cut (tenderloin / top round, ~6% fat). Chips: 1 large russet (~300 g) fried in canola — estimated ~38 g oil absorbed. Macros shown are the full plate (tartare + chips + lettuce); the tartare alone is ~344 kcal / 28 g protein per serving. Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. RAW BEEF + RAW EGG — see her safety flags. Estimate.

serving_desc: ½ the tartare (~140 g) + ½ the chips + lettuce — a starter-sized main

ingredients.note: must be very fresh, high-quality and kept cold — eaten raw

steps: Slice the beef ~3 mm thick, lay on parchment and freeze until semi-firm.
Meanwhile finely chop the shallot, gherkins, capers, parsley and chives.
Dice the semi-frozen beef into ~3 mm cubes, keeping it on the cold tray as you work.
In a chilled bowl whisk Dijon, lemon, olive oil, Tabasco and Worcestershire until emulsified; fold in the beef, shallot, parsley, gherkins and capers. Season and adjust.
Plate on a chilled plate, top with chives and the egg yolk; serve with fried potato chips and lettuce leaves.

batch_totals.note: Full plate for 2. The deep-fried chips are nearly half the calories (~590 kcal, ~38 g fat for the batch). Tartare alone (no chips/lettuce): ~687 kcal / 56.5 g protein / 47.7 g fat for 2 — ~8.2 g protein per 100 kcal.

him.verdict: The tartare itself is a strong, zinc-rich protein dish: ~28 g protein per serving with lean beef's zinc, iron and B12 (zinc is a top sperm-priority micro), and ~8.2 g protein per 100 kcal. What drags it down is the plate around it — deep-fried chips add ~295 kcal and ~19 g fat per serving, and 2 tbsp olive oil in the dressing makes the tartare itself fat-forward. Eaten raw, food-safety depends entirely on the beef's freshness and handling.
flags: tartare alone: ~28 g protein / ~344 kcal per serving, rich in zinc, iron, B12
deep-fried chips ≈ half the plate's calories
2 tbsp olive oil + raw yolk make the tartare fat-forward
raw beef — needs very fresh, well-handled meat
suggested_mods: Swap the fried chips for oven-baked or air-fried potato wedges (spray oil) — saves ~200+ kcal per serving
Cut the dressing oil to 1 tbsp — the Dijon and lemon still emulsify
Lean on the lettuce cups for scooping instead of chips
Buy the beef from a butcher who knows it's for tartare; keep everything ice-cold and eat immediately

her_preconception.verdict: Not suitable for her once trying or pregnant, as written: both the beef and the egg yolk are RAW. Raw/undercooked meat carries toxoplasmosis, E. coli and Listeria risk, and raw yolk carries salmonella risk — all serious in pregnancy. The advisory approach (trying within ~6 months, not yet) means it's fine for her now if she wants it, but it should come off the menu once actively trying.
prenatal_highlights: iron, zinc, B12 (beef) — but only safe in a cooked form

safety_advisories.note: RAW BEEF — toxoplasmosis / E. coli / Listeria risk in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: cook it: the same seasoning works as a seared beef 'tartare-style' patty or quickly seared diced beef

safety_advisories.note: RAW EGG YOLK — salmonella risk in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: omit, or use a pasteurized yolk

suggested_mods: Once trying/pregnant, skip this or make a fully cooked version

cooking_guide: Use the freshest, highest-quality lean beef you can get, ideally cut to order and labeled for raw consumption; keep it refrigerated until the last moment.
Semi-freezing (firm but not hard) is the key to clean, even 3 mm dice — soft beef smears instead of cutting.
Hand-dice rather than mince: a sharp knife keeps the texture distinct; a grinder makes it pasty.
Work cold throughout — chilled bowl, cold tray, cold plate — both for safety and so the fat doesn't smear.
Whisk the dressing until it emulsifies BEFORE adding the beef, then fold gently and season at the end; taste and adjust acid and salt.
For the chips, slice the potato thin and even, rinse off the starch and dry thoroughly before frying, so they crisp instead of steaming.
Plate and serve immediately — tartare shouldn't sit at room temperature.
